hooks.text: A truck-sized space rock skipped off Earth's atmosphere like a stone.
A meteor dipped to an altitude of fifty-eight kilometers and survived.
An asteroid bounced off our planet's atmosphere and escaped back into space.

title: The Asteroid That Skipped Off Earth
description: On August 10, 1972, a massive meteoroid skipped off Earth's atmosphere over Utah and bounced back into deep space.

beats.text: A truck-sized space rock skipped off Earth's atmosphere like a stone.
beats.visual: Artist's concept of an Earth-grazing meteor skipping off Earth atmosphere, 1972
queries: meteoroid skipping off Earth atmosphere artist's impression

beats.text: On August 10, 1972, the Great Daylight Fireball entered the sky over Utah at thirty-three thousand miles per hour.
beats.visual: Daylight fireball smoke trail in the blue sky over western United States, 1972

beats.text: The object streaked fifteen hundred kilometers northward, visible in broad daylight across the western United States and Canada.
beats.visual: Western United States and Canada relief map highlighting Utah to Alberta trajectory
queries: Western United States and Canada relief map
Utah Wyoming Montana Alberta map highlights

beats.text: During its pass, the meteoroid dipped to a minimum altitude of just fifty-eight kilometers.
beats.visual: Earth atmosphere layers altitude diagram highlighting mesosphere at 58km

beats.text: Witnesses in Montana reported hearing a startling double sonic boom as the rock rushed overhead.
beats.visual: Diagram of sonic boom shockwave cones from supersonic object, 1972

beats.text: The entire frantic encounter lasted approximately one hundred seconds.
beats.visual: U.S. military Defense Support Program satellite in Earth orbit, 1972

beats.text: The dense atmosphere acted like a cosmic ramp, stripping away half the object's mass and warping its orbital tilt from fifteen degrees to seven.
beats.visual: Diagram showing the change in celestial mechanics orbital inclination degrees, 1972

beats.text: Having bounced off our sky and escaped back into space, the Great Daylight Fireball was never seen again.
beats.visual: NASA artist's concept of an Apollo-type near-Earth asteroid in deep space, 1972
